## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paṭibāhana Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 27) is an ecclesiastical rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating the communal distribution of robe material among Buddhist nuns [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. According to the rule, a nun who obstructs or blocks a legitimate and appropriate distribution of robe-cloth commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In the canonical origin narrative, the nun Thullanandā creates an obstacle to the community's acquisition of robes (*cīvaralābhaṃ antarāyaṃ akāsi*) [Hüsken 1997]. Subsequent casuistry in the commentary and analysis specifies that obstructing the receipt of other monastic requisites constitutes a lesser offense of wrongdoing (*dukkaṭa*) [Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that this rule has no direct parallel in the Pātimokkha rules for monks [Hüsken 1997]. It has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the corresponding rule in the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, as well as the Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions preserved in Chinese and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Machine-assisted alignments from DharmaNexus confirm cross-language matches with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (Degé D0005) and Vinaya Vibhaṅga literature [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali Canon, DharmaNexus identifies extensive textual reuse with adjacent and related Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga training rules, particularly Pācittiyas 29, 26, 53, 47, and 30 [DharmaNexus].
